title: KS-1556 follow-up (#1529 round-2 gate m1): four rotate-chain guards have no behavioural cell (M10 owner-only cleanup, M3b retire exactly the returned ids, M7 grace memory expiry, M1 tenant-scoped key), plus ROTATE_CHAIN_WAIT_MS parses '10s' as 10 ms
description:
## BLUF

**Four guards in the KS-1556 rotate chain and its post-COMMIT apply are not pinned by any behavioural cell.** The code is correct today; a refactor could regress the chain's stated purpose **silently**. Test gap only — no product defect measured, and no credential-validity outcome depends on any of these (every validate on the DB path decides on the stored row). Found by the round-2 Opus delta gate on PR #1529 as its Minor **m1** (verdict sha256/16 `b662a71501b66490`, at head `d19b7a708e5b`). Facts only; no build.

## The four guards (lines at `d19b7a708e5b`, `services/security/src/index.ts`)

| mutant | guard | survives | consequence (by reading) |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| **M10** | `:302` `if (rotateChains.get(key) === mine) rotateChains.delete(key);` — only the OWNER of a chain entry removes it | all 26 author cells, the chain unit file and the gate's 19 cells | rotate A runs, B is queued; A finishes and deletes **B's** entry; a rotate C arriving while B runs finds no predecessor, takes a pooled client and parks on the advisory lock. That is the pool pressure the chain exists to prevent (KS-757): the gate's CH6 shows an unrelated validate waiting 1.6 s with 2 clients free, and a 503 once `connectionTimeoutMillis` (5 s) passes. Memory ordering is unaffected. **Availability.** |
| **M3b** | `:377` `for (const id of retiredIds ?? [])` — memory retires **exactly the ids the database RETURNED** | everything | if a concurrent non-rotate mint of the same connector commits after the retire's snapshot, the mutant retires that key in memory while the DB keeps it active; validate's "revoked if either says so" then **refuses a valid key** in this process. Fail-closed. **Availability.** |
| **M7** | `:379` `retireInMemory(current, grace)` — the **grace** path's post-COMMIT memory expiry | every author cell (killed only by the gate's A6) | memory keeps no expiry the DB committed; cosmetic on the DB path, because validate re-reads the stored row. |
| **M1** | the chain key is `${tenantId}:${connectorId}` — two tenants with the same connector id are independent | caught **only** by the window cell's literal `chains.has(\`${TENANT}:${c}\`)\` string — an implementation assertion | behaviour pinned only by the gate's CH5. |

## The cells the gate suggests (owner's call)

1. **Chain:** A in flight and B queued; after A finishes, issue C and assert C **waits for B**, with **0** service backends on `wait_event = 'advisory'` (kills M10).
2. **Pool pressure** like the gate's CH6.
3. **Grace 60:** after a 201, assert the prior key's memory entry **carries the expiry** (kills M7).
4. **Two tenants, one connector id:** behaviourally independent, like CH5 (pins M1 without reading the key string).
5. For M3b: a concurrent non-rotate mint landing after the retire's snapshot keeps its key active in memory.

## Folded in: o6 (cosmetic hardening, same function)

`:279-281` `rotateChainWaitMs()` uses `Number.parseInt(process.env.ROTATE_CHAIN_WAIT_MS)`, so `ROTATE_CHAIN_WAIT_MS=10s` **parses as 10 ms** — effectively no chain, and the CH6 pool pressure returns. A unit-suffixed value should be refused or parsed, not silently truncated.

## Related

KS-1556 (the PR this follows up), KS-1549 (the parent), KS-757 (the pool trap the chain prevents).

nodes.title: Refs KS-1568: ROTATE_CHAIN_WAIT_MS must be a plain number of milliseconds (o6)

nodes.body:
**BLUF: item o6 is merged as #1628 (develop `390cc0a317c9`). A unit-suffixed `ROTATE_CHAIN_WAIT_MS` such as `10s` no longer shrinks the rotate-chain wait to 10 ms; any value that is not a plain number of milliseconds falls back to the 10-second default. Nothing is deployed, so this ticket stays In Progress.**

**The reading chosen is "refuse", not "parse".** `1e3` and `250.5` are refused as well, and develop read them as 1 ms and 250 ms. If `10s` should mean 10 seconds instead, that is a product decision this change did not make.

**Two cells were added to the Spark pass.** The original five cells would still have passed if the fix were swapped for a plain `Number()`, so nothing pinned the "refuse" reading. W6 and W7 now do.

**Still open:**
* The large-value edge in my earlier comment. Gate AQ1 confirmed it independently: above about 24.8 days the timer fires after roughly 1 ms. No tracked config sets this variable.
* This ticket's main items, the four rotate-chain guards with no behavioural cell (M10, M3b, M7, M1), are untouched.

**BLUF: item o6 is raised as #1628 (at gate AQ1). One edge of the same problem is NOT fixed by it, and is recorded here because this ticket owns the rotate-chain wait.**

**The edge: a very large `ROTATE_CHAIN_WAIT_MS` also means "no chain".** Node's `setTimeout` cannot wait longer than 2,147,483,647 ms (about 24.8 days). Any longer delay is clamped to **1 ms**, with only a `TimeoutOverflowWarning`.

* I measured it on Node v24.7.0: `2147483648` and `3000000000` both waited **1 ms**.
* Develop's reader and #1628's reader both **accept** those values, because they are plain digits and greater than 0.
* So someone who sets a large wait meaning "wait a long time" gets no chain at all. That is the same failure as `10s` reading as 10 ms, reached by a different value.

**Why it is not in #1628:** the PR raises the held Spark pass faithfully, and the edge is older than it. The fix is one condition in `rotateChainWaitMs()`, `raw <= 2_147_483_647` (anything larger falls back to the default), plus one cell.

The ticket's main items (the four rotate-chain guards with no behavioural cell: M10, M3b, M7 and M1) are untouched by #1628.
